title: Marked flat modules on split square-zero base changes
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use all module sheaves on the small etale ringed sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the specified tensor pullbacks and units [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], their tensor-normalized composition [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] and identity comparison [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback], and the normalized geometric ring and module stalks [def-sfb-space-geometric-stalk-models]. For a $k$-vector space $V$ with its central right action, use the actual split square-zero base $D_V=\operatorname{Spec}(k\oplus V)$ and its augmentation and maps induced by linear maps from [def-sfb-marked-curve-deformations]. Regard these schemes as the representable algebraic spaces of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Define $X_V=X\times_k D_V$ as the sheaf product over the terminal base sheaf; it is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Retain its projections $p_V:X_V\to X$ and $b_V:X_V\to D_V$ and its special-fibre inclusion $i_V:X\to X_V$. A linear map $f:V\to W$ induces $c_f:X_W\to X_V$, identity on $X$, with $i_Wc_f=i_V$ and $p_Vc_f=p_W$.
For $M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, a marked flat module over $V$ is an $\mathcal O_{X_V}$-module $N$, flat at every geometric stalk over the geometric local ring of $D_V$ via $b_V$, together with an isomorphism $\alpha:i_V^*N\cong M$. Flatness is Module.Flat after restriction along the specified ring-stalk map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Marked isomorphisms commute with $\alpha$ after tensor pullback. Define its class set to be the quotient by marked isomorphism. Define tensor-pullback relations using the actual functor $c_f^*$ and marking $i_W^*c_f^*N\cong i_V^*N\xrightarrow{\alpha}M$ from the normalized composition comparison. A trivial marked module is marked-isomorphic to $p_V^*M$, marked by $i_V^*p_V^*\cong\mathrm{id}$. Define $\operatorname{Aut}^0_V(M)$ to be the automorphisms of $p_V^*M$ sent to the identity by $i_V^*$. Pullback of such automorphisms uses conjugation by the normalized $c_f^*p_V^*M\cong p_W^*M$. For $V=k\times k$, a gluing of two marked modules over $k$ is a marked flat module whose tensor restrictions under the two coordinate projections give those modules; no existence or uniqueness of gluing is included in this definition. Relabelling a marking by $e:M\cong M'$ means postcomposing it with $e$.
In the derived category of all modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], computed on the equivalent small affine etale model, write $\operatorname{Ext}^n(M,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(M[0],M[0][n])$. For $a\in k$, the scalar endomorphism of $M$ is the unique map multiplying every chart section by the pullback of $a$ from $k$. Its derived shifted postcomposition is the usual scalar action on Ext. Relabelling Ext by $e$ is precomposition by $e^{-1}[0]$ and postcomposition by $e[0][n]$. These define the objects and operation relations; vector-space laws and the classification are separate assertions.
